# Add a late thought without derailing the current work

Use this utility when you remember an important addition after a task has started. It captures the addition and folds it into the current work only where it belongs.

## When to use it

Use `also` for a late constraint, correction or extra detail. Do not use it to secretly replace the current objective. If you want to stop or change direction, say that directly.

## What you need

You need the addition in plain language and the context of the active task. The agent decides whether it refines remaining work, becomes a follow-up, or requires a recompile.

## Try it

Slash-command harnesses:

```text
/also For HarborTasks export, empty result sets should still produce a header row.
```

Codex equivalent:

```text
$also For HarborTasks export, empty result sets should still produce a header row.
```

## What happens

The skill appends the addition to the active prompt context without restarting the whole workflow. If the addition changes the goal or invalidates work already done, the agent must surface that instead of pretending nothing changed.

## What you get

Illustrative output shape:

```text
Addition captured.
Effect: updates acceptance criteria for the export spec.
No current implementation has started, so no rework is required.
```

## Review before continuing

Check whether the addition changes the done-when or not-in-scope. A late “also build import” is a new task, not an addition to export.

## Tips and recovery

If the agent chases the addition and forgets the original goal, ask it to restate the active goal and where the addition landed. If the addition is consequential, consider [compile](#skill-compile).

## Where to go next

Continue the active workflow, or use [prompts](#skill-prompts) and [searchprompts](#skill-searchprompts) if the addition was meant to reuse an earlier request.
